evals.name: greenfield-spring-kotlin
evals.prompt: The directory evals/opentelemetry-workspace/fixtures/spring-kotlin is a Kotlin Spring Boot app with two Maven modules, mvc (Web MVC with suspend service functions and an @Async AuditJob) and webflux (Mono-returning services). It has no telemetry. This app must support OpenTelemetry; wire it fully in the mvc module and prove it works. The service name is fixture-spring-kotlin.
expectations: Uses the Micrometer path (Actuator, Micrometer Tracing with the OpenTelemetry bridge, OTLP registry/exporters) rather than the raw OpenTelemetry SDK or the Java agent
Export is configured only through standard OTEL_* environment variables (placeholders such as ${OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT} in application.yaml); no endpoint or sampler is hard-coded in code
W3C tracecontext and baggage propagation are configured and both enabled

Resource attributes service.name, service.version and deployment.environment.name are set from OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES; verification fails (or the agent says it must) if service.name is unset rather than shipping unknown_service

Service and repository beans get Tier 2 spans through a class-level aspect (ServiceObservationAspect or equivalent) named ClassName.method with code.namespace and code.function.name; no spans on the controller
The aspect records the default metrics app.service.calls (counter) and app.service.duration (histogram, unit s) with the outcome attribute
The coroutine hop in the suspend service function keeps the parent span (OpenTelemetry Kotlin context element and MDCContext, or equivalent context propagation)
The @Async AuditJob runs as its own root span with a span link to the triggering request span, not as a child
The OpenTelemetry Logback appender is installed alongside a console pattern that includes trace_id and span_id

Component tests use in-memory span, log record and metric exporters and assert: descendant order of service and repository spans, outbound client span with same-trace server span, coroutine hop keeps parent, log carries trace_id and span_id, default metrics, no ERROR on happy path and one on failure, job link
Exactly one Testcontainers integration test starts a collector container with the file exporter config and asserts spans, logs and metrics arrived and that a log carries a span's trace ID
A compose file for local viewing is added, with host ports read from environment variables with standard defaults
The app is shown to start and serve requests with no collector reachable, or the agent explains the SDK's non-blocking export behaviour
No library version numbers appear in any instructions or prose outside the project's build file
The agent does not claim done without running the component and integration tests and reporting their results

evals.name: greenfield-nuxt
evals.prompt: The directory evals/opentelemetry-workspace/fixtures/nuxt is a Nuxt 4 app (Nitro node-server preset, Nitro tasks enabled) with OrderService, OrderRepository, PricingClient and an audit task. It has no telemetry. This app must support OpenTelemetry; wire it fully and prove it works. The service name is fixture-nuxt.
expectations: Initialises the OpenTelemetry Node SDK in a --import preload file (for example instrumentation.mjs) loaded before the server, and states why: Nitro plugins load after the HTTP server and database modules are imported, so they cannot patch them
Export is configured only through standard OTEL_* environment variables; no endpoint or sampler in code; HTTP/protobuf OTLP by default
W3C tracecontext and baggage propagators are configured; resource carries service.name, service.version and deployment.environment.name, and verification fails if service.name is unset

A withSpan helper (exported from a server utils module) wraps public methods of services and repositories with span name ClassName.method, code.namespace and code.function.name; no spans on route handlers
withSpan records app.service.calls and app.service.duration (unit s) with an outcome attribute
The audit task started with runTask opens its own root span with a span link to the triggering request span
pino is used with the OpenTelemetry pino instrumentation so log records carry trace_id and span_id, and logs are exported over OTLP; console output stays readable and LOG_FORMAT selects JSON
The SDK flushes and shuts down on SIGTERM with a bounded timeout
Batch processors are used on this long-lived server, with export failures not crashing the app

vitest component tests use in-memory span, log record and metric exporters and assert the same list as the Spring template (parentage order, client span with same-trace server span, async hop keeps parent, log correlation, default metrics, error status rules, job link)
Exactly one Testcontainers integration test runs a real collector with the file exporter and asserts spans, logs and metrics arrived and that a log carries a span's trace ID
A compose file for local viewing is added
No package version numbers appear in instructions or prose outside package.json
The agent does not claim done without running the tests and reporting their results

evals.name: review-pr-propagation-and-loops
expectations: Flags the hand-built fetch that does not carry trace context headers as High (or Critical if framed as context lost across a process boundary), noting that the ledger side will start a new trace; suggests using the auto-instrumented client or injecting the propagator headers
Flags the per-item span inside the for loop as High and recommends one span with an item.count attribute (plus a span only around the batch), unless the body is shown to do IO worth individual bars
Flags the log line as High: it is not correlated (module-level logger instead of the request child logger) and interpolates the invoice id and status into the message instead of passing fields
Flags @WithSpan on the controller as Low (the server span already covers the handler)
Notes the span in the loop is never ended on error (no try/finally) or that invoice.id as a span attribute is acceptable while an ID in a span name or metric attribute would not be
Every finding carries a severity tag from Critical, High, Medium, Low
Findings cite file and line or hunk and give a concrete fix
Does not cite the skill by name in the output
States a clear verdict rather than only a list

evals.name: metrics-design-trap
evals.prompt: We are adding metrics to our order service (Spring Boot, Kotlin) so ops can see how it is doing. I was thinking of a counter called orders_total with an order_id label so we can find a specific order, a gauge for how many orders are open right now, and a timer for how long placing an order takes in milliseconds. Give me the metric definitions and the Kotlin code to register them.
expectations: Rejects the order_id attribute (high cardinality) and explains that individual orders are found through traces or logs, not metric attributes
Renames the counter to orders.placed (dotted lowercase, domain first, no plural noun, no _total suffix) and explains that the backend adds suffixes
Uses an up-down counter for the open-orders level that rises and falls, rather than a plain counter, and notes a gauge is for sampled values the app does not own
Records order placement duration as a histogram in seconds (UCUM unit s), not milliseconds, and not a gauge
Suggests a histogram for order value with a UCUM-appropriate unit if value is measured, or notes the unit must be stated
Uses only low-cardinality attributes (for example outcome, payment method category), none of which is an ID, email or free text
Mentions that Tier 2 service methods already emit the default metrics app.service.calls and app.service.duration, so duplicate timers on the same methods are not needed
Registers the instruments through Micrometer on Spring while keeping OpenTelemetry-style names, and does not hard-code an exporter endpoint

evals.name: nuxt-serverless-preset
evals.prompt: Our Nuxt 4 app deploys to a serverless platform (Nitro preset for a Lambda-style runtime, with a variant for an edge runtime). It must support OpenTelemetry. How should I wire it? Give the file layout and code.
expectations: Does not use a batch span or log processor; uses simple processors that export immediately, or calls forceFlush on every signal before the invocation returns, because the process can freeze at any time
Flushes per invocation (for example in a Nitro afterResponse hook or equivalent) and does not rely on a SIGTERM shutdown hook or a periodic metric reader timer
States that the --import preload flag is not available on serverless and replaces it with explicit SDK initialisation at module load
Names which Node auto-instrumentations are unavailable on the edge runtime and gives manual fetch instrumentation or context propagation as the alternative there
Uses a streaming export path if the platform offers one, or says it checked
Export still configured only through OTEL_* environment variables with OTLP over HTTP/protobuf; no vendor SDK; W3C propagators on
Sets service.name, service.version and deployment.environment.name and fails loudly if service.name is missing
Keeps the app serving requests when the collector is unreachable (short export timeout, errors logged once)
